operations.description:
Register a new guest user for anonymous browsing access to the discussion board platform.

This endpoint creates a guest account identified by a unique device fingerprint, enabling temporary session management without requiring traditional email/password authentication. The device fingerprint is generated from browser/device characteristics to distinguish anonymous visitors. If no fingerprint is provided, the system generates one automatically.

The operation creates a new record in the discussion_board_guests table with the device_fingerprint field set to the provided or generated value. It also creates an initial session record in discussion_board_guest_sessions with connection metadata including the client IP address, initial page URL (href), and HTTP referrer header for traffic source tracking.

Upon successful registration, the endpoint returns JWT access and refresh tokens in the IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized response structure. The access token grants temporary browsing permissions, while the refresh token enables session renewal before expiration. Session expiration is configured according to platform policy and stored in the expired_at column of the guest session record.

Guests have read-only access to sections, articles, and comments but cannot create content, manage profiles, or access member-only features. This operation is the entry point for anonymous users to access the discussion board platform.

operations.description:
Refresh an existing guest session to obtain new JWT access and refresh tokens.

The system verifies that the session's expired_at timestamp has not passed, ensuring the session is still active. If the session is found and valid, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated with fresh expiration times according to the platform's session duration policy.

The session record in discussion_board_guest_sessions is updated with the new expired_at timestamp to extend the session lifetime. This enables guests to maintain their browsing session across extended periods of activity without losing their anonymous identity.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or not found, the operation returns an authentication error indicating the guest must re-join to obtain new credentials. This ensures expired sessions are properly terminated and prevents unauthorized access using stale tokens.

This session captures the client's IP address, the page URL where authentication was initiated (href), and the HTTP referrer header value for security auditing purposes. The access token provides short-term authentication for API requests, while the refresh token enables token renewal without re-authentication. operations.description:

This endpoint validates administrator credentials against the discussion_board_members and discussion_board_admins tables. The authentication process first verifies the email address exists and retrieves the associated member record. It then validates the provided password against the stored password_hash using secure comparison algorithms.

The operation performs multiple validation checks: confirming the member account status is 'active' (not suspended or deleted), verifying an associated administrator record exists in discussion_board_admins, ensuring the administrator record has deleted_at null (indicating active administrator status), and checking the administrator is not currently banned.

Upon successful authentication, the system generates a pair of JWT tokens: an access token for immediate API authentication and a refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication. A session record is created in discussion_board_admin_sessions capturing the discussion_board_admin_id, IP address, referrer URL, and href for audit trail compliance. The session's expired_at timestamp enforces token validity periods.

This endpoint is part of the complete authentication flow alongside /auth/admin/join for registration and /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal. Administrators use this endpoint to establish authenticated sessions for accessing moderator capabilities including section management, content deletion, user banning, and admin request processing.

operations.description:

The operation validates the provided refresh token against existing sessions in the discussion_board_admin_sessions table, ensuring the session record exists and is associated with a valid administrator account.

The refresh process performs several validation checks: verifying the refresh token matches a valid session, confirming the session's expired_at timestamp is in the future (session not expired), validating the associated administrator record in discussion_board_admins has deleted_at null (active administrator), and checking the linked member account status remains 'active'.

Upon successful validation, the operation generates a new JWT access token with updated expiration. Depending on security configuration, it may also issue a new refresh token with a rotated value to prevent token replay attacks. The session's expired_at timestamp is updated to extend the session duration according to the configured session policy.

This endpoint is essential for maintaining continuous administrator sessions during extended platform governance activities. It works in conjunction with /auth/admin/login which initially issues the refresh token. The stateless JWT architecture means logout is handled client-side by discarding tokens - no server-side logout endpoint is required.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of member accounts from the discussion board platform.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for discovering user profiles across the platform. Users can search by display name using partial matching, filter by account status (active, suspended, deleted), and navigate through results using cursor-based pagination. The endpoint supports sorting by registration date (newest or oldest first) to help users find recently joined members or browse the community chronologically.

For guests and regular members, this endpoint enables profile discovery and community exploration. Each result includes essential profile information: display name, bio preview, account status, and registration timestamp. The summary format optimizes list display performance while providing sufficient context for users to identify profiles of interest.

Administrators have enhanced capabilities through this endpoint, including the ability to filter by all account statuses for user management purposes. This supports administrative workflows such as reviewing suspended accounts, monitoring community growth, and identifying users for potential administrative actions.

The operation integrates with the profile viewing system - users can retrieve detailed profile information including article and comment history by using the member ID obtained from this list in the GET /members/{memberId} endpoint. Search results respect privacy and access control policies, ensuring appropriate visibility based on the requesting user's authorization level.

Validation ensures search queries meet length requirements and pagination parameters stay within configured limits. The endpoint handles edge cases including empty result sets, invalid status filters, and concurrent account state changes gracefully.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_members table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply search filters on display_name using trigram similarity for partial matching (GIN index on display_name). Filter by status field (active, suspended, deleted) - guests and members can only see active accounts, administrators can see all statuses.

Support cursor-based pagination using created_at timestamp for efficient large dataset navigation. Default page size 20, maximum 100 items per page.

Join with discussion_board_admins to enrich results with administrator grade information for admin users viewing the list.

Exclude soft-deleted accounts (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from results for non-administrator users. Administrators can optionally include deleted accounts for audit purposes.

Handle concurrent account status changes by reading consistent snapshots. Apply row-level security based on requesting user's role.

Return IDiscussionBoardMember.ISummary for each member containing: id, display_name, bio (truncated), status, created_at, and isAdmin flag.

Retrieve a specific member's public profile information by their unique identifier.

This operation returns comprehensive profile data including the member's display name shown publicly on articles and comments, biography text for personal description, and account status indicating active, suspended, or deleted state. The profile also includes temporal metadata such as account creation timestamp and last update timestamp.

The endpoint supports public profile viewing accessible to all actors including guests, members, and administrators. Guests can browse profiles without authentication as part of public content discovery. Members can view other members' profiles to see their discussion contributions. Administrators can view profiles for moderation and user management purposes.

Sensitive authentication fields such as email address and password hash are intentionally excluded from the response to protect user privacy and security. The profile response focuses on publicly shareable information that facilitates community interaction and user discovery within the discussion board platform.

Related operations include PATCH /members for retrieving the authenticated user's own profile with additional details, PATCH /members/{memberId}/articles for listing articles written by the member, and PATCH /members/{memberId}/comments for listing comments posted by the member.

Query discussion_board_members table by primary key UUID.

Validate memberId is valid UUID format. Return 404 if member not found or if deleted_at is not null (soft deleted account).

Cache profile data with appropriate TTL to reduce database load for frequently viewed profiles.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's profile information including display name and biography text.

This operation allows authenticated members to modify their profile by updating their display name and bio text stored in the discussion_board_members table. The display name is a required field shown publicly on articles, comments, and profile pages - visible to all users including guests. The bio text is an optional personal description visible on the member's profile page.

The operation requires authentication with a valid member session token and only allows members to update their own profile. Attempting to update another user's profile will be rejected with an authorization error. The display name field must be provided in every update request and is validated against character limits and content restrictions. The bio field is optional and can be omitted, set to null, or updated with new text content.

Profile changes are reflected immediately across all content authored by the member, including articles and comments where the display name appears. The updated_at timestamp in the discussion_board_members table is automatically updated to the current timestamp when the profile is modified.

Validation rules applied:
- Display name: Must meet character limits and content restrictions defined in User Validation Rules
- Bio text: Must not exceed maximum length defined in User Validation Rules

Related operations include GET /discussionBoard/member/profile for viewing the current user's profile and PATCH /discussionBoard/members for searching and viewing other users' profiles.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the authenticated member's profile in the discussion_board_members table.

1. Extract member ID from authenticated session token
2. Validate request body:
   - display_name: required, must be non-empty string
   - bio: optional, can be null or string
3. Validate display_name meets content policies (no prohibited content)
4. Update discussion_board_members record:
   - SET display_name = request.display_name
   - SET bio = request.bio (or keep existing if not provided)
   - SET updated_at = current timestamp
5. Return updated member record with new profile data
6. Handle concurrent update conflicts with optimistic locking

Authentication: Requires valid member session token. Guest users and administrators must authenticate as members to update their profile.

The response includes administrator summary information optimized for list displays, showing the administrator's grade level, promotion date (created_at), and associated member display name. This enables administrators to understand the current administrator hierarchy and identify peers for collaboration on platform governance tasks.

Only active administrators are included in the results - records with deleted_at set (soft-deleted administrators whose privileges were revoked) are excluded. The deleted_at field being null indicates an active administrator, while a non-null deleted_at timestamp indicates the administrator privileges have been revoked.

This operation requires administrator authentication as per the admin actor definition with platform governance capabilities. Regular members and guests cannot access the administrator list. The endpoint supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options by grade level, promotion date, or member display name.

Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator account.

This operation returns comprehensive administrator profile data including the administrator's grade level (regular or super), associated member account information, and account lifecycle timestamps. The administrator grade determines privilege scope: regular administrators can manage sections, delete content, and ban users; super administrators have elevated powers including approving admin requests and managing other administrators' grades.

The response includes the administrator's ID, grade level, creation timestamp, last update timestamp, and the associated member's profile information (email, display name, bio, account status). This endpoint is useful for viewing administrator details, verifying administrator status, and displaying administrator profiles to authorized users.

Administrators are promoted from existing members through an approval process, maintaining a 1:1 relationship with the original member account. The administrator record preserves the member's identity while granting elevated permissions. If the administrator has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null), the operation will return a 404 error indicating the administrator is no longer active.

This operation requires administrator authentication. Only users with administrator role can access this endpoint to view administrator account details. This restriction ensures that sensitive administrator information including grade levels and account lifecycle data is only visible to authorized personnel with platform governance responsibilities.

4. Return the administrator record with embedded member data (display_name, bio, email, status)

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of discussion board articles from the discussion_board_articles table with comprehensive search and sorting capabilities.

This operation provides article discovery functionality including text search across title and content fields, filtering by section (discussion_board_section_id), tags (via discussion_board_article_tags junction table), and author (discussion_board_member_id). The endpoint supports offset-based pagination for efficient navigation through result sets.

Search functionality utilizes PostgreSQL gin_trgm_ops trigram indexes on title and content columns for efficient text matching. Tag filtering matches articles that have any of the specified tags through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table. Section filtering restricts results to articles within a specific discussion_board_sections record.

Each article in the response includes essential summary information: title, author details (joined from discussion_board_members), associated tags, comment count (aggregated from discussion_board_comments), and created_at timestamp. The full content field is not included in list results to optimize performance and reduce payload size.

Authorization: Available to all actors (guest, member, admin). Banned users cannot access this endpoint. Articles with deleted_at timestamp populated are automatically excluded from results (soft delete filtering).

Related operations: GET /articles/{articleId} retrieves full article details including content and attachments. PATCH /sections/{sectionId}/articles filters articles by a specific section.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_articles table with pagination, search filters, and sorting.

Search Implementation:
- Use PostgreSQL gin_trgm_ops trigram indexes on title and content for efficient text search
- Apply ILIKE pattern matching for search queries
- Support combined title/content search when both provided

Filtering Logic:
- Section filter: WHERE discussion_board_section_id = {sectionId}
- Tag filter: JOIN discussion_board_article_tags and discussion_board_tags, filter by tag names
- Author filter: WHERE discussion_board_member_id = {authorId}
- Exclude soft-deleted: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

Sorting Options:
- 'newest': ORDER BY created_at DESC (default)
- 'oldest': ORDER BY created_at ASC

Pagination:
- Implement cursor-based pagination using created_at and id for stable ordering
- Support configurable page size with reasonable limits (e.g., 10-100 items per page)
- Return pagination metadata: total count, current page, has_next, has_previous

Response Assembly:
- Join with discussion_board_members for author display name
- Aggregate tags via discussion_board_article_tags junction
- Count comments via discussion_board_comments with GROUP BY
- Map to IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary DTO

Edge Cases:
- Empty search query returns all articles (no filtering)
- Non-existent section/tag/author returns empty result set
- Handle concurrent article deletion during query gracefully

operations.description:
Create a new discussion board article with title, content, section assignment, and optional attachments.

This operation enables authenticated members to create articles within the discussion board system. Each article must be assigned to exactly one section for topic organization and categorization. The article serves as the foundation for community discussion and debate on various topics.

The creation process supports multiple file attachments and image attachments through URI references. File attachments store metadata including original filename, MIME type, and file size for proper download handling. Image attachments include dimension information (width and height) for optimal display rendering.

operations.specification:
Create a new article record in discussion_board_articles table with the following steps:

1. Validate authentication: Ensure request is from authenticated member (discussion_board_members). Reject guest users with 401 Unauthorized.

2. Validate section existence: Query discussion_board_sections by provided sectionId. Return 404 Not Found if section doesn't exist or is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null).

3. Validate required fields:
   - title: non-empty string, minimum 1 character, maximum 200 characters
   - content: non-empty string, minimum 1 character, maximum 100000 characters
   - sectionId: valid UUID format

4. Validate optional attachments:
   - fileUrls: array of valid URI strings (string & tags.Format<"uri">)
   - imageUrls: array of valid URI strings (string & tags.Format<"uri">)
   - tags: array of non-empty strings, deduplicate before processing

5. Create article record:
   - Generate new UUID for article id
   - Set discussion_board_section_id from request
   - Set discussion_board_member_id from authenticated session
   - Set title and content from request
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
   - Set deleted_at to null

6. Process file attachments (if fileUrls provided):
   - For each file URL, create discussion_board_article_files record
   - Extract filename from URL or use provided metadata
   - Set discussion_board_article_id to new article's id
   - Set discussion_board_member_id from session
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp

7. Process image attachments (if imageUrls provided):
   - For each image URL, create discussion_board_article_images record
   - Extract or compute image dimensions (width, height)
   - Set discussion_board_article_id to new article's id
   - Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp

8. Process tags:
   - For each unique tag name:
     a. Query discussion_board_tags by name (case-insensitive)
     b. If exists, use existing tag id
     c. If not exists, create new tag with generated UUID and current timestamp
     d. Create discussion_board_article_tags record linking article and tag

9. Return complete article entity with all relationships loaded:
   - Article base fields (id, title, content, timestamps)
   - Section information (joined from discussion_board_sections)
   - Author information (joined from discussion_board_members)
   - File attachments array (from discussion_board_article_files)
   - Image attachments array (from discussion_board_article_images)
   - Tags array (joined through discussion_board_article_tags to discussion_board_tags)

Transaction boundary: Steps 5-8 must execute within a single database transaction. If any step fails, rollback all changes to maintain data consistency.

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: User not authenticated as member
- 404 Not Found: Section not found or deleted
- 400 Bad Request: Validation errors (missing required fields, invalid formats)
- 500 Internal Server Error: Database transaction failure

Soft delete the discussion_board_sections record by setting deleted_at to current timestamp.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify requesting user has administrator privileges
2. Query discussion_board_sections by sectionId, excluding already deleted records
3. Validate section exists and is not already deleted
4. Check if any articles exist in discussion_board_articles with this section_id and deleted_at IS NULL
5. If articles exist, reject with 409 Conflict error
6. Update section: set deleted_at = NOW()
7. Return success response

Transaction scope: Single table update on discussion_board_sections.

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: Section does not exist or already deleted
- 409 Conflict: Section contains articles
- 403 Forbidden: Non-administrator attempting deletion

Authorization: Requires admin actor role.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of historical snapshots for a specific discussion board section.

This operation provides access to the audit trail of section modifications, allowing administrators to track how a section's name and description have changed over time. Each snapshot represents an immutable, point-in-time capture of the section's state, created automatically when section modifications occur.

The snapshots are stored in the discussion_board_section_snapshots table, which maintains an append-only history linked to the parent section through the discussion_board_section_id foreign key. Each snapshot preserves the name and description values as they existed at the time of capture, along with the created_at timestamp indicating when the snapshot was recorded.

This endpoint supports filtering by date range to help administrators review changes within specific time periods. Results are paginated to handle potentially large historical records efficiently. The snapshots are indexed by discussion_board_section_id and created_at for optimal query performance.

Access to section snapshots is restricted to administrators only, as this audit trail data is used for compliance, moderation review, and change tracking purposes. Regular members and guests cannot access historical section data.

The sectionId path parameter must correspond to an existing section in the discussion_board_sections table. If the section has been soft deleted (deleted_at is not null), snapshots may still be accessible for audit purposes depending on business rules.

This operation provides access to historical section data captured at specific moments for audit trail, compliance review, and change tracking purposes. Each snapshot is immutable and represents the exact state of a section (name and description) at the time it was created, as defined in the `discussion_board_section_snapshots` table.

Snapshots are automatically generated when sections are modified, creating an append-only history of all changes. This endpoint allows administrators to review past section configurations, verify when changes occurred, and maintain transparency in platform governance. The snapshot record includes the `id` (unique identifier), `discussion_board_section_id` (reference to the parent section), `name` (section name at snapshot time), `description` (section description at snapshot time), and `created_at` (timestamp when the snapshot was captured).

This operation provides tag search functionality enabling users to discover existing tags when creating or editing articles. Supports partial name matching for tag autocomplete scenarios, allowing users to find relevant tags by typing partial text. The search is case-insensitive to improve discoverability.

Tags are system-managed entities automatically created when users first use them on articles. Each unique tag name is stored once in the discussion_board_tags table and referenced by multiple articles through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table. This design enables efficient tag reuse and prevents duplication.

The response includes tag summaries with essential information: tag ID (UUID format), tag name, and creation timestamp. Results are paginated to handle large tag collections efficiently, with configurable page sizes and sorting options.

This endpoint is accessible to all actors (guest, member, admin) as tag discovery is a fundamental feature for content browsing and article creation workflows. Guests can browse tags to explore content topics, while members use tags during article creation and editing.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query discussion_board_tags table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply partial name matching on the name column using case-insensitive comparison. Support prefix matching for autocomplete scenarios (e.g., searching 'poli' matches 'Politics', 'Political').

Implement cursor-based or offset pagination with configurable page size (default 20, max 100). Sort results by name alphabetically or by created_at descending (most recently used tags first).

Join with discussion_board_article_tags to optionally include article count per tag for popularity indication.

Handle edge cases: empty search returns all tags, special characters in search query are escaped, duplicate consolidation already handled at storage level.

Validate search query length (max 50 chars to match tag name limit). Return 400 for invalid pagination parameters.

This operation returns the complete tag entity including the tag name, creation timestamp, and last update timestamp. Tags are reusable categorization labels that enable efficient article filtering, search, and content discovery workflows across the discussion board.

Tags are created on-demand when users add them to articles and can be reused across multiple articles through the discussion_board_article_tags junction table. Each unique tag name is stored once in the discussion_board_tags table with a uniqueness constraint preventing duplication.

This endpoint is accessible to all actors including guests, members, and administrators. Tag information is public metadata used for article categorization and discovery. The tag's article associations can be explored through related article list endpoints filtered by this tag.

Related operations include PATCH /articles for tag-based article filtering and GET /articles/{articleId} which displays tags associated with individual articles.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of content snapshots for a specific article, providing a complete audit trail of how the article's title and body have changed over time.

This operation is restricted to administrators and returns point-in-time snapshots from the discussion_board_article_snapshots table that are automatically created by the system whenever an article is created or modified. Each snapshot captures the exact state of the article's title and body content at that moment, enabling content moderation review, compliance auditing, and change tracking.

Snapshots are immutable audit records that cannot be created, modified, or deleted by users through API operations. They are managed automatically by the system to maintain a complete historical record. The snapshots are sorted by creation timestamp, allowing administrators to trace the evolution of article content from its initial creation through all subsequent edits.

The endpoint supports filtering by date range to focus on specific time periods, and pagination to handle articles with extensive edit histories. Each snapshot entry includes the captured title, body content, and the timestamp when the snapshot was created.

This operation requires administrator privileges as it accesses audit trail data used for platform governance and content moderation. The snapshot history provides transparency into content changes and supports compliance requirements. Administrators can review snapshot data even for soft-deleted articles to maintain complete audit trails.

Query discussion_board_article_snapshots table filtered by discussion_board_article_id matching the path parameter.

Apply pagination with cursor-based or offset-based approach for large result sets. Default sorting by created_at ascending (oldest first) to show chronological evolution, with option to reverse sort.

Support date range filtering on created_at field to limit results to specific time periods. Join with discussion_board_articles to verify article exists and user has access permission.

Return snapshot summary data including id, title, body, and created_at. Ensure soft-deleted articles are handled appropriately - snapshots may still be accessible for audit purposes even if parent article is soft-deleted.

Validate that the requesting user has permission to view the article (article author, section access, or administrator). Apply rate limiting to prevent excessive audit trail queries.

Retrieve a specific point-in-time snapshot of an article's content from the discussion_board_article_snapshots table.

This operation returns the historical state of an article at a particular moment, including the title and body content as they existed when the snapshot was created. Snapshots are stored in the discussion_board_article_snapshots table and are automatically generated when articles are created or modified to maintain a complete audit trail for compliance and content moderation purposes. Each snapshot is linked to its parent article through the discussion_board_article_id foreign key relationship.

The snapshot entity has a "snapshot" stance, meaning it supports read-only operations. Snapshots are immutable once created and preserve the exact content state at the time of capture. Each snapshot includes the creation timestamp (created_at) indicating when the state was recorded.

Access to article snapshots requires administrator privileges. The parent article must be accessible (not soft-deleted) for the snapshot to be retrievable. If the parent article has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is populated in discussion_board_articles table), the snapshot cannot be accessed through this endpoint. This operation is part of the administrative audit and compliance workflow.

operations.description:
Retrieve the edit history snapshots for a specific comment within an article.

This operation provides access to the complete audit trail of comment modifications. Each snapshot represents a point-in-time capture of the comment's content, created automatically whenever the comment is edited. Snapshots are immutable and append-only, ensuring a complete historical record for content moderation review and audit compliance.

The endpoint requires both the article ID and comment ID in the path to establish proper context and access control. This dual-parameter structure ensures snapshots are accessed within their correct parent article context, matching the denormalized storage design where snapshots reference both the parent comment and article for historical accuracy.

Supports comprehensive filtering and pagination capabilities including date range filtering by snapshot creation time, content search, and member-based filtering. Results are returned in chronological order with configurable page sizes for efficient browsing of edit histories.

Access is available to all authenticated users for comments they authored, and administrators can view snapshots for any comment. Guest users cannot access snapshot history. The operation respects soft deletion states - snapshots of deleted comments remain accessible for audit purposes.

Each snapshot represents an immutable record of the comment's state at a specific point in time, automatically created by the system whenever a comment is edited.

The endpoint requires administrator authentication and is part of the admin audit trail review functionality. Administrators can view snapshots to track comment content changes, verify edit history, and investigate content moderation issues.

Snapshots preserve the exact content text, author member ID, associated article ID, and creation timestamp. The three-level path hierarchy (article → comment → snapshot) ensures proper data integrity and access scoping.

This operation is restricted to administrators only. Regular members and guests cannot access comment snapshot data. The response includes complete snapshot information for audit and moderation purposes.

operations.description:
Submit an administrator application request for privilege escalation from member to administrator role.

This operation allows authenticated members to request administrator privileges by providing a justification reason. The system creates a new admin request record with initial status set to 'pending' and associates it with the submitting member's account. The request is then placed in the pending queue for super administrator review.

Members can only have one pending administrator request at a time. If a member already has a pending request, the system rejects the new submission with a conflict error. Members who already hold administrator privileges cannot submit admin requests. Once submitted, requests cannot be withdrawn or edited by the member.

The reason text must be between 50-2000 characters and provide sufficient justification for the administrator privilege request. The system records the submission timestamp for sorting the pending queue and enforcing waiting periods between rejected requests.

Super administrators review pending requests using the GET /admin-requests endpoint and process them using PUT /admin-requests/{adminRequestId}/approve or PUT /admin-requests/{adminRequestId}/reject operations. Upon approval, the member is promoted to regular administrator status.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new administrator application request in the discussion_board_admin_requests table.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate the authenticated user is a member (not guest, not already admin)
2. Check if the member already has a pending request by querying discussion_board_admin_requests where member_id equals current user and status equals 'pending'
3. If pending request exists, return 409 Conflict error
4. Validate reason text: required, 50-2000 characters, no prohibited content
5. Create new discussion_board_admin_requests record with:
   - id: generated UUID
   - member_id: current authenticated member's ID
   - admin_id: null (not yet decided)
   - reason: validated reason text
   - status: 'pending'
   - submitted_at: current timestamp
   - decided_at: null
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
6. Return the created request entity with full details

Transaction scope: Single table insert operation, no complex transaction needed.

Error handling:
- 401 Unauthorized: User not authenticated
- 403 Forbidden: User is guest or already has admin privileges
- 409 Conflict: Member already has pending request
- 400 Bad Request: Reason text validation failure (too short, too long, invalid content)

responseBody.description: Created administrator request with pending status

requestBody.description: Administrator application request submission with justification reason

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of administrator application requests.

This operation provides super administrators with the ability to view administrator requests submitted by members seeking privilege escalation. The endpoint supports filtering by request status (pending, approved, rejected), date range filtering by submission time, and comprehensive pagination.

The primary use case is for super administrators to access the queue of pending requests awaiting review. Each request includes the member's justification reason, submission timestamp, current status, and decision information if applicable.

Authorization is restricted to super administrators only. Regular administrators cannot view the pending requests list or process admin requests. Regular members can only view their own requests through a separate endpoint. Super administrators should filter by status 'pending' to see requests awaiting their review decision.

Results are sorted by submission timestamp to maintain the first-come-first-served review order. The response includes pagination metadata for navigating large result sets.

Apply status filter to retrieve requests by state (pending/approved/rejected). Support date range filtering on submitted_at column for temporal queries. Join with discussion_board_members table to include member display name and email in response.

For pending requests, join with discussion_board_admins is not needed. For decided requests, optionally join to include deciding administrator information.

Implement cursor-based or offset pagination based on system configuration. Default page size should be 20 items. Support sorting by submitted_at ascending (oldest first) for pending queue management.

Validate that requesting user has administrator privileges. Super administrators can view all requests; regular administrators may have restricted access based on business rules.

Handle edge cases: empty result sets, invalid status filters, date range validation. Return 403 for non-administrator access attempts.

Join with discussion_board_admins if admin_id is populated to include deciding administrator details. Return complete request record including reason, status, submitted_at, decided_at timestamps. Authorization check: allow access if requesting user is the submitting member OR has administrator role. Return 404 if request not found or access denied. Include request history entries from discussion_board_admin_request_histories if available for audit trail context.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator application request by its unique identifier.

This endpoint provides complete visibility into an administrator privilege escalation request, including the member's justification reason, current approval status, submission timestamp, and decision metadata if processed. The response includes the submitting member's profile information and, if decided, the reviewing administrator's details.

Authorization is granted to two actor types: the member who submitted the request can view their own request at any time, and administrators can view all requests for review and processing purposes. When a request has been approved or rejected, the response includes the decision timestamp and the administrator who made the determination.

The operation queries the discussion_board_admin_requests table and joins with related member and administrator records to provide comprehensive context. Request status values are: pending (awaiting super administrator review), approved (member promoted to administrator), or rejected (request denied). Status transitions from pending to approved/rejected are immutable per business rules.

Related operations include PATCH /admin-requests for listing pending requests with filtering, POST /admin-requests/{requestId}/approve for approval actions, and POST /admin-requests/{requestId}/reject for rejection actions.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the administrator application request to retrieve (UUID format, global scope)

responseBody.description: Complete administrator application request details including submitter information, justification reason, current status, and decision metadata

operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update an administrator application request by changing its status from pending to approved or rejected.

Service layer logic:
1. Validate the requesting user is a super administrator
2. Query discussion_board_admin_requests table by requestId
3. Verify request exists and current status is 'pending'
4. Validate new status is either 'approved' or 'rejected'
5. Check unique constraint: ensure no conflicting status exists for this member
6. Update the record: set status, admin_id (current super admin), and decided_at (current timestamp)
7. Trigger status transition: if approved, promote member to regular administrator grade
8. Create audit trail entry in discussion_board_admin_request_histories table
9. Return the updated request entity

Business rules:
- Only super administrators can update admin requests
- Can only update requests with 'pending' status
- Status transitions are immutable: pending → approved/rejected (cannot be changed after decision)
- admin_id must be set to the deciding super administrator's ID
- decided_at must be set to the decision timestamp
- If approved, automatically create administrator record for the member with regular administrator grade

Edge cases:
- Request not found: return 404
- Request already decided (status is approved/rejected): return 409 Conflict
- Requesting user is not super administrator: return 403 Forbidden
- Invalid status value: return 400 Bad Request
- Concurrent update conflict: use optimistic locking with updated_at timestamp
operations.description:
Update an administrator application request by approving or rejecting it.

This operation allows super administrators to review and decide on pending administrator application requests submitted by members. The decision changes the request status from 'pending' to either 'approved' or 'rejected', records the deciding administrator's ID, and timestamps the decision.

When a request is approved, the submitting member is automatically promoted to regular administrator status with elevated platform governance privileges. When rejected, the member remains at their current role level. Status transitions are immutable - once a decision is made (approved or rejected), it cannot be changed or reversed through this endpoint.

The operation enforces strict authorization: only super administrators can approve or reject requests. Regular administrators, members, and guests cannot access this endpoint. The system maintains a complete audit trail through the decided_at timestamp and administrator request history records.

Related operations:
- PATCH /admin-requests: List pending administrator requests for super administrator review
- GET /admin-requests/{requestId}: Retrieve detailed information about a specific request
- POST /admin-requests: Members submit new administrator application requests

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete audit history of status transitions for an administrator application request.

This operation provides full transparency into the admin request review process by returning all recorded status changes from submission through final decision. Each history entry captures the status at that point in time, which super administrator made the decision, the timestamp of the transition, and optionally the rejection reason if the request was denied.

The audit trail includes the initial pending status when the member submitted the request, followed by the final decision (approved or rejected) made by a super administrator. This endpoint supports the platform's commitment to administrative transparency and accountability in privilege escalation workflows.

Access is restricted to super administrators only, as the history contains sensitive information about administrative decisions and personnel. Regular administrators and members cannot view this audit trail. The requesting administrator must have super administrator grade privileges as defined in the discussion_board_admins.grade field.

The histories are returned in chronological order by default (oldest first), showing the complete lifecycle from submission through decision. Pagination is supported for systems with extensive audit trails, though typically an admin request will have only 2-3 history entries (pending → approved/rejected).

Related operations: GET /admin-requests/{requestId} retrieves the current state of the admin request. PATCH /admin-requests provides list of all requests with filtering by status.

Apply pagination parameters (page, limit) from request body. Default sorting by created_at ascending (oldest first) to show chronological progression.

Return the complete history record including id, discussion_board_admin_request_id, deciding_admin_id, status, reason (nullable), and created_at timestamp. operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific administrator request status transition from the audit trail.

This operation returns a single history entry that captures when an administrator application request's status changed, which super administrator made the decision, and the reason for rejection if applicable. Each history entry provides complete transparency into the privilege escalation workflow and supports administrative audit compliance requirements.

The history entry includes the status at the transition point (pending, approved, or rejected), the deciding super administrator's ID, optional rejection reason text, and the exact timestamp when the transition occurred. This information is essential for understanding the complete lifecycle of an administrator application request.

Access to this audit trail is restricted to administrators with appropriate permissions. The operation validates that the specified historyId exists and belongs to the admin request identified by requestId, ensuring data integrity and preventing unauthorized access to audit records.

Related operations: GET /discussionBoard/admin/admin-requests/{requestId} should be used to retrieve the parent request details, while this operation focuses specifically on individual status transition records within the audit trail.

operations.description:
Update an administrator's grade level between regular administrator and super administrator.

This operation is restricted to super administrators only. Regular administrators cannot access this endpoint even though they have the 'admin' role. The operation enables super administrators to manage administrator grades by promoting regular administrators to super administrator or demoting other super administrators to regular administrator.

The grade field determines the scope of administrative privileges: regular administrators can manage sections, delete content, and ban users, while super administrators have additional powers including approving admin requests and managing other administrators' grades. Grade changes are immediately effective upon update.

The operation enforces the critical business rule that super administrators cannot demote themselves to prevent losing all elevated privileges on the platform. When attempting self-demotion, the system rejects the request with 403 Forbidden. All grade changes are recorded in the discussion_board_admin_audit_logs table for compliance and security auditing.

The target administrator must exist and be active (deleted_at is null). Soft-deleted administrator records cannot be modified. After grade change, the administrator immediately gains or loses the corresponding capabilities.

This operation is part of the administrator grade management workflow defined in requirements sections 15, 117, and 166. Super administrators should use PATCH /admins to view the list of administrators and their current grades before performing grade changes. Related operations include GET /admin-requests for pending administrator applications and POST /admin-requests/{requestId}/approve for approving new administrators.
operations.name: updateGrade
operations.specification:
Update the grade field of discussion_board_admins record identified by adminId.

Implementation steps:
1. Verify caller has super administrator grade (query discussion_board_admins where member_id equals authenticated user's id and grade equals 'super' and deleted_at is null)
2. Verify adminId is not the caller's own admin record (prevent self-demotion)
3. Verify target admin record exists and is active (deleted_at is null)
4. Validate grade value is either 'regular' or 'super'
5. Update discussion_board_admins record: set grade to new value, set updated_at to current timestamp
6. Return updated admin record with full details

Edge cases:
- Self-demotion attempt: reject with 403 Forbidden
- Target admin not found: reject with 404 Not Found
- Target admin already deleted: reject with 404 Not Found
- Caller not super admin: reject with 403 Forbidden
- Invalid grade value: reject with 400 Bad Request

Transaction: Single table update on discussion_board_admins. Consider logging grade change to discussion_board_admin_audit_logs for audit trail.

responseBody.description: Updated administrator record with new grade level and updated_at timestamp reflecting the grade change.

requestBody.description: New grade level for the administrator. Must be either 'regular' or 'super'. Self-demotion (super admin changing own grade to regular) is prohibited and will be rejected.

prerequisites.description: Administrator must be approved and created in the system before their grade level can be updated. This operation creates the administrator record by approving a pending admin request.

This supports administrative oversight and accountability in ban enforcement.

Administrators can filter results by user information (display name or email), search within ban reason text, and filter by ban date ranges. The response includes pagination metadata to navigate through large result sets.

This endpoint requires administrator authentication. Regular members and guests cannot access ban information. The ban list serves as the authoritative source for tracking all active access restrictions on the platform.

Retrieve detailed information about a specific ban record.

This operation provides administrators with complete ban details including the ban reason, timestamp when the ban was imposed, and references to both the banned member and the enforcing administrator. The ban information supports administrative transparency and accountability in platform governance.

The endpoint returns the full ban entity with all fields from the discussion_board_bans table, including the immutable banned_at timestamp and the required ban reason that was recorded when the ban was imposed. Soft-deleted records (unbanned users) are excluded from results.

Only administrators have access to this endpoint. Regular members and guests cannot view ban details. This restriction ensures that sensitive moderation information remains within the administrative team while maintaining the transparency required for platform governance.

operations.description:
Create a new ban record to restrict a user's access to the platform.

This operation allows administrators to ban a member account, preventing the user from logging in while preserving visibility of their existing articles and comments. The ban requires a mandatory reason text that explains the justification for the access restriction, supporting administrative transparency and audit requirements.

When executed, the system automatically records the ban timestamp and associates the ban with the executing administrator's account. The banned user's account status is updated to reflect the access restriction, blocking all authentication attempts while maintaining content visibility per the content preservation policy.

Only administrators have permission to execute this operation. The system validates that the target user exists, is not already banned (enforced by unique constraint on member_id), and that the ban reason meets minimum and maximum length requirements. Duplicate ban requests for already-banned users are rejected.

Related operations: GET /bans retrieves the list of banned users with ban reasons. DELETE /bans/{banId} removes a ban to restore user access. The ban creation is part of a transaction boundary that updates both the ban record and the member's access status atomically.
operations.name: create

Verify target member exists and is not already banned (check unique constraint on member_id). Validate ban reason meets length requirements (minimum and maximum). Auto-generate admin_id from authenticated administrator context. Auto-generate banned_at timestamp. Insert ban record with member_id, admin_id, reason, and banned_at. Update member status if needed. Return created ban record with all fields. Handle duplicate ban rejection via unique constraint violation. Transaction boundary includes ban record creation and member status update.

operations.description:

When a request is approved, the system transitions the request status from pending to approved, records the approving super administrator's identity and decision timestamp, and automatically creates a regular administrator account for the applicant.

The operation enforces strict validation rules: the request must exist and be in pending status, the applicant must not already hold administrator privileges, and the calling user must be a super administrator. If multiple super administrators attempt to approve the same request simultaneously, the system ensures only one approval succeeds through transaction isolation.

Upon successful approval, the applicant gains regular administrator capabilities including section management, content deletion, user banning, and content moderation. The approved request record is preserved for audit trail purposes with the decided_at timestamp and admin_id fields populated.
